title_en: Wang Gaowu v. Yunji Road Securities Business Department — stock dispute
keywords_en: Civil; Stock Dispute; Second Instance; Intermediate People's Court; Hubei Province; Natural Person; Financial Institution; Determination of Liability for Unauthorized Sale of Stocks; Compliance of Securities Business Department Operating Procedures; Sufficiency of Evidence; Affirmation of Original Judgment; Clearing of Stock Account Password; Stocks Sold; Funds Withdrawn; ID Card Not Lost; Securities; Yunji Road Securities Business Department Stock Dispute
full_text_en:
Wang Gaowu v. Yunji Road Securities Business Department — stock dispute

Plaintiff: Wang Gaowu, male, 31 years old, employee of China Chemical Engineering No. 16 Construction Company, residing in Yichang City, Hubei Province.

Agent ad litem: Liu Kun and Qin Aiguo, lawyers of Hubei Chengye Law Firm.

Defendant: Yichang Yunji Road Business Department, Wuhan Branch, Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd. Domicile: Yichang City, Hubei Province.

Representative: Zhang Xiaoming, manager of the business department.

Agent ad litem: Guo Jingwen, staff member of Yichang Yunji Road Business Department, Wuhan Branch, Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd.

Agent ad litem: Chen Xiaochi, lawyer of Hubei Tianyi Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Wang Gaowu, filed a lawsuit with the Xiling District People's Court of Yichang City, Hubei Province, due to a stock dispute with the Yichang Securities Trading Business Department of Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd. During the litigation, Wang Gaowu requested to change the name of the defendant to Yichang Yunji Road Business Department, Wuhan Branch, Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yunji Road Business Department).

The plaintiff alleged: In August 1999, the password of the plaintiff's stock account opened at the defendant's premises was reset, four stocks were sold, and RMB 83,000 in the funds account was withdrawn, while the plaintiff was on a business trip elsewhere. For this reason, the plaintiff repeatedly contacted the defendant to discuss the matter. The defendant not only refused to compensate but also falsely accused the plaintiff of colluding with others, and in newspaper reports claimed that the plaintiff was present at the scene and involved in the case, causing significant mental harm to the plaintiff. The plaintiff prayed for an order that the defendant compensate the plaintiff for the losses from the unauthorized sale of stocks and unauthorized withdrawal of funds, as well as the plaintiff's lost wages and travel expenses incurred in dealing with the matter, pay mental damages of RMB 30,000, publish an apology in relevant newspapers, and bear the litigation costs of this case.

The defendant argued: 1. The entity that the plaintiff sued has already been dissolved; 2. The password reset, sale, and cash withdrawal were all carried out in strict accordance with the business department's procedures and were handled by the plaintiff himself. The plaintiff's claims are unfounded and should be dismissed.

The facts found by the Xiling District People's Court of Yichang City after trial were as follows:

On November 18, 1996, the plaintiff Wang Gaowu filled out an account opening registration form at the Yichang Huaxia Securities Registration Center and opened a Shenzhen securities account and a Shanghai securities account. On the same day, the former "Yichang Securities Trading Business Department of Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd." (the predecessor of the defendant in this case) became Wang Gaowu's designated securities trading agent by signing a designated trading agreement with Wang Gaowu. Wang Gaowu obtained a self-service magnetic card (MAC) and began stock trading. As of August 5, 1999, Wang Gaowu's stock account held 500 shares of Fengle Seed, 1,210 shares of Jifa Co., Ltd., 400 shares of Guotou Yuanyi, and 3,200 shares of Gree Electric Appliances. On that day, Wang Gaowu went to the defendant Yunji Road Business Department with his own ID card and securities account card to go through the password reset procedures. On August 6, the above four stocks were sold by self-service magnetic card, with a transaction amount of over RMB 83,500. On the same day, Wang Gaowu went through the large-sum withdrawal reservation procedures at Yunji Road Business Department and filled out a reservation form, stating the withdrawal date as August 9 and the cash to be withdrawn as RMB 83,500. The name filled in on the large-sum withdrawal reservation form and the withdrawal slip was Wang Gaowu, and the ID number and securities account number filled in were also those used by Wang Gaowu, but the handwriting was not Wang Gaowu's. Wang Gaowu claimed that he had been on a business trip to Shandong from August 7 and only discovered the problem with his stock account on the 28th of the same month, whereupon he rushed back. After returning, he inquired at Yunji Road Business Department and learned that his password had been reset on August 6, the four stocks in his account had been sold, and a large-sum withdrawal reservation form had been filled out in his name, with RMB 83,000 in cash withdrawn on the 9th of the same month. Yunji Road Business Department argued that every transaction conducted by the department was strictly in accordance with the "Operational Procedures for Agency Business" of the Wuhan Branch of Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd. From password reset, trading, to cash withdrawal, if the customer did not personally present the ID card, shareholder code card, and provide the funds account number, it would be impossible to access the account via the computer and handle the transaction. Therefore, the transactions handled for Wang Gaowu on August 5, 6, and 9, 1999, were all conducted by him in person with the required documents, and the department and bank staff strictly reviewed and verified the documents before processing.

The plaintiff Wang Gaowu's claims for compensation for lost wages and travel expenses were not supported by conclusive evidence.

It was also found that the plaintiff Wang Gaowu's shareholder code card, ID card, and self-service magnetic card MAC had never been lost and had been turned over by Wang Gaowu to the public security department. On October 21, 1999, the "Sanxia Evening News" published a report titled "80,000 Yuan of Stock Funds Disappear into Thin Air," followed by two subsequent follow-up reports. The above reports merely described the incident and the reflections of some shareholders, without expressing any opinions or analyses.

It was further found that, with the approval of the administrative authority for industry and commerce, the legal person status of the Yichang Securities Trading Business Department of Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd. was canceled on April 8, 1997. This change did not involve the placement of original personnel or changes in equipment, facilities, and debts, etc. The newly registered enterprise name was "Yichang Business Department, Wuhan Branch, China Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd."

On December 24, 1999, the "Yichang Business Department, Wuhan Branch, China Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd." was again changed to the current defendant's name, "Yichang Yunji Road Business Department, Wuhan Branch, Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd."

The above facts were confirmed by evidence including the plaintiff Wang Gaowu's ID card, securities account, self-service magnetic card MAC, large-sum withdrawal reservation form, withdrawal slip, stock transaction flow sheet for August 6, 1999, entrustment inquiry sheet, inquiry sheet from the Enterprise Registration and Administration Sub-bureau of Yichang Administration for Industry and Commerce, statements of the parties, and witness testimony.

The Xiling District People's Court of Yichang City held that:

After the legal person qualification of "Yichang Securities Trading Business Department of Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd." was canceled, its personnel, equipment, facilities, and debts were all merged into the newly registered enterprise legal person. Therefore, the defendant Yunji Road Business Department in this case should bear liability for the debts of the former "Yichang Securities Trading Business Department of Huaxia Securities Co., Ltd." The plaintiff Wang Gaowu's application to change the defendant's name should be granted.

The plaintiff Wang Gaowu's ID card and shareholder code card were both in his possession and had never been lost. His claim that the stocks were stolen by another person based solely on the fact that the handwriting was not his own, and his request for an order that the defendant Yunji Road Business Department compensate him for his economic losses, lacked sufficient evidence and was not supported. Wang Gaowu's claims for compensation for lost wages, travel expenses, and mental damages were also not supported due to lack of factual basis and legal basis. Accordingly, the Xiling District People's Court of Yichang City rendered the following judgment on May 31, 2000:

All claims of the plaintiff Wang Gaowu were dismissed.

Litigation costs of RMB 4,910 were borne by the plaintiff Wang Gaowu.

Wang Gaowu, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Yichang Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province. The reasons were: (1) The trial court's finding that the appellant himself handled all procedures and withdrew the funds, based solely on the testimony of the appellee Yunji Road Business Department's staff, who had an interest in the case, was erroneous. Furthermore, the trial court's finding that the password reset occurred on August 5, 1999, and that the "Sanxia Evening News" only reported the incident and the reflections of some shareholders, were inconsistent with the facts; (2) The appellant had provided conclusive and sufficient evidence to support his claims. Under these circumstances, the trial court's dismissal of the appellant's claims on the ground of insufficient evidence was improper. The appellant requested the reversal of the original judgment and a new judgment ordering Yunji Road Business Department to compensate the appellant for the capital loss of RMB 83,000, mental damages of RMB 30,000, and other losses of over RMB 15,000, and to publish an apology in the newspaper.

The appellee Yunji Road Business Department argued: The trial court's findings were clear and the application of law was correct. The appellate court should dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The facts found by the Yichang Intermediate People's Court upon retrial in the second instance were as follows:

The trial court's findings regarding the evolution and name changes of the appellee Yunji Road Business Department were confirmed.

On August 4, 1999, the appellant Wang Gaowu withdrew RMB 1,000 from his account. As of this date, Wang Gaowu's account held 500 shares of Fengle Seed, 1,210 shares of Jifa Co., Ltd., 400 shares of Guotou Yuanyi, 3,200 shares of Gree Electric Appliances, and cash of RMB 53.45. From August 7 to 29, 1999, Wang Gaowu was on a business trip to Zhucheng Chemical Fertilizer Plant in Shandong Province and returned to Yichang on the 29th. On August 30, Wang Gaowu went to the comprehensive counter of the appellee Yunji Road Business Department and stated that when he swiped his magnetic card to operate his account during his business trip to Shandong, the computer always prompted a password error, and he requested an inquiry. Upon inquiry at the comprehensive counter, it was found that the password of Wang Gaowu's account had been reset on August 6, and all the stocks in the account had been sold on the same day, with a transaction amount of RMB 84,090.60; on the same day, a large-sum withdrawal reservation form was filled out in Wang Gaowu's name, reserving a withdrawal of RMB 80,000; and on August 9, cash of RMB 83,000 was withdrawn from Wang Gaowu's account. Wang Gaowu claimed that the Yunji Road Business Department's irregular operations had caused him property losses and demanded compensation. Yunji Road Business Department refused, stating that every transaction was conducted strictly in accordance with procedures and that the RMB 83,000 was taken by Wang Gaowu himself. A dispute arose, and Wang Gaowu filed the lawsuit.

It was further found that, upon the application of the appellee Yunji Road Business Department, the Yichang Public Security Bureau issued handwriting identification reports on October 30, 1999, and August 29, 2000, respectively, under document numbers Yi Shi Gong Guo Bao Ji Zi (1999) No. 27 and (2000) No. 20, concluding that the handwriting on the large-sum withdrawal reservation form for August 6, 1999, and the withdrawal slip for August 9, 1999, in Wang Gaowu's account, was written by one person, but not by Wang Gaowu or his wife Zheng Xiaohong.

The Yichang Intermediate People's Court held that:

The focus of the dispute in this case was whether the password reset, stock sale, and fund withdrawal were conducted by the appellant Wang Gaowu himself. Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A party has the responsibility to provide evidence for its own claims." Wang Gaowu submitted to the trial court evidence that the signatures were not his own and that he was not in Yichang on the dates of the reservation and the withdrawal, to support his claim that "it was not done by Wang Gaowu." The appellee Yunji Road Business Department submitted testimony from its internal employees to support its claim that "it was done by Wang Gaowu" and argued that if it were not Wang Gaowu, how could the ID number and shareholder code on the reservation form and withdrawal slip match those used by Wang Gaowu? Evaluating the evidence submitted by both parties comprehensively: Wang Gaowu's evidence was consistent with the handwriting identification report issued by the public security department, which was collected by the court during the trial. Therefore, Wang Gaowu should be considered to have met his burden of proof for the claim that "it was not done by Wang Gaowu." The evidence from Yunji Road Business Department not only lacked sufficient probative value because it came from internal employees with an interest in the case but also could not be accepted because it contradicted the handwriting identification conclusion. Even if the ID card and shareholder code card were never lost, the ID number and shareholder code were not absolutely confidential information unknown to others besides the holder himself. Therefore, the consistency of the numbers on the withdrawal reservation form and withdrawal slip with those used by Wang Gaowu could not prove that "it was done by Wang Gaowu." To use this argument to refute the other party, Yunji Road Business Department needed to submit conclusive evidence. This was not Wang Gaowu's claim, and the burden of proof for "why they were consistent" could not be shifted to Wang Gaowu. Yunji Road Business Department, lacking sufficient evidence to prove that "it was done by Wang Gaowu," could only have its claim deemed unsubstantiated.

Furthermore, according to the "Operational Procedures for Agency Business" implemented by the appellee Yunji Road Business Department, for a customer to reset a password, the customer must personally present his/her ID card and shareholder code card, fill out a password reset application form, and have the operator carefully review before processing. Therefore, after the password reset procedure, the password reset application form filled out by the customer would be evidence that Yunji Road Business Department should and could provide. Yunji Road Business Department's failure to provide the password reset application form to prove its claim not only further indicated that its claim was unsubstantiated but also showed that it did not carry out the password reset in accordance with the prescribed procedures. A password is a means of protecting investors' rights and interests, and resetting a password involves the interests of investors. Yunji Road Business Department's failure to follow the prescribed procedures for the password reset created the conditions for the funds in Wang Gaowu's account to be withdrawn. Yunji Road Business Department should bear liability for this fault.

The "Operational Procedures for Agency Business" also provided that for a customer to withdraw margins, the customer should personally present the original ID card and shareholder code card, and the person making the withdrawal should sign the withdrawal slip. Accordingly, it should be considered that the person who signed the withdrawal slip was the customer himself or an authorized agent of the customer with a power of attorney. On the withdrawal slip for August 9 submitted by the appellee Yunji Road Business Department, although the name signed was "Wang Gaowu," it was not written by the appellant Wang Gaowu himself. Moreover, the withdrawal slip did not attach Wang Gaowu's power of attorney, nor did it contain the name and ID number of an agent. This fact proved that Yunji Road Business Department was negligent in its review of documents when handling the large-sum withdrawal reservation and withdrawal business in this case.

Article 106, paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Citizens and legal persons who breach a contract or fail to perform other obligations shall bear civil liability." Article 117, paragraph 1 provides: "If state property, collective property, or the property of another person is encroached upon, it shall be returned; if it cannot be returned, compensation shall be made at an estimated price." Paragraph 3 provides: "If the victim suffers other major losses as a result, the infringer shall also compensate for those losses." Article 192 of the Securities Law also provides: "If a securities company violates a client's instructions in buying or selling securities, handling transaction matters, or handles other matters contrary to the client's true intent, thereby causing losses to the client, it shall bear compensation liability according to law and shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 100,000."

The appellee Yunji Road Business Department, as the designated agent of the appellant Wang Gaowu, had the duty to ensure the safety of the stocks and funds in Wang Gaowu's account. Yunji Road Business Department handled the agency business irregularly, failing to conduct strict review and complete the relevant procedures, and carelessly carried out the password reset, large-sum withdrawal reservation, and withdrawal business for Wang Gaowu's account. This resulted in the sale of stocks from Wang Gaowu's account and the withdrawal of funds. In the absence of sufficient evidence to confirm that "it was done by Wang Gaowu" or "it was done by someone authorized by Wang Gaowu," Yunji Road Business Department should compensate Wang Gaowu for the withdrawn funds and bear interest losses at the one-year bank deposit interest rate of 2.25% per annum. Additionally, Yunji Road Business Department should also appropriately compensate Wang Gaowu for the lost wages and related travel expenses incurred in dealing with the dispute.

The appellant Wang Gaowu's claim that the appellee Yunji Road Business Department's statements published in the "Sanxia Evening News" caused him mental harm and that Yunji Road Business Department should pay him mental damages pertains to a different legal relationship from this case and falls outside the scope of this lawsuit.

In summary, some of the appellant Wang Gaowu's grounds for appeal were well-founded and should be sustained. The first-instance judgment incorrectly found the facts due to shifting the burden of proof, leading to an erroneous decision, and should be reversed. Accordingly, in accordance with Items (2) and (3) of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Yichang Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 9, 2000:

1. The first-instance civil judgment is reversed;
2. The appellee Yunji Road Business Department shall compensate the appellant Wang Gaowu for the capital loss of RMB 83,000, interest of RMB 2,173 for the period from August 9, 1999, to October 9, 2000, and appropriately compensate Wang Gaowu for travel expenses and lost wages in the amount of RMB 500, totaling RMB 85,673, to be fulfilled within 10 days after this judgment takes effect.

First-instance litigation costs of RMB 4,910 shall be borne by the appellee Yunji Road Business Department in the amount of RMB 3,683 and by the appellant Wang Gaowu in the amount of RMB 1,227. Second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 3,780 shall be borne by Yunji Road Business Department in the amount of RMB 2,835 and by Wang Gaowu in the amount of RMB 945.
